Every command of greenlens with its options and examples. The same text is available offline with 'greenlens help &lt;command&gt;'.

## Global options

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--config` | Configuration file. Defaults to /etc/greenlens/greenlens.yaml, then the file of the user |  |
| `--lang` | Language for messages (code: en or es). Defaults to the system locale |  |
| `--no-color` | Do not color the output; NO_COLOR has the same effect |  |
| `-o`, `--output` | Output format (format: table, json, csv or yaml) | `table` |
| `-q`, `--quiet` | Print only the result, without progress or advice |  |
| `--raw` | Show values in base units (J, W, g) with full precision |  |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | Print details of every step, such as sensor read errors |  |

## greenlens agent

Run the agent in the foreground: it samples the energy sources, stores the measurements and serves the other commands through its local socket. Under systemd it runs as the greenlens service. SIGHUP reloads the configuration and SIGTERM stops it.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens agent [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens agent
greenlens agent --config /etc/greenlens/greenlens.yaml
```

## greenlens calibrate

Measure the power of every domain while the machine is idle and store the median as the idle baseline. The dynamic idle policy subtracts this baseline before attributing energy to processes. Stop other workloads first.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens calibrate [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--duration` | How long to measure | `1m0s` |
| `--interval` | Sampling interval (default: agent.sample_interval) |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens calibrate
greenlens calibrate --duration 5m
```

## greenlens measure

Measure the energy used while a command runs, while a process and its children run, or while a systemd unit runs, and attribute to it the share of CPU and memory energy that matches its CPU time. With a command, its exit code becomes the exit code of measure and the report goes to standard error.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens measure [-- command] [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--duration` | Stop after this time; by default, when the target ends |  |
| `--interval` | Sampling interval (default: agent.sample_interval) |  |
| `--pid` | Measure this process and its children |  |
| `--report` | Write the report to this file instead of the terminal |  |
| `--unit` | Measure this systemd unit |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens measure -- ollama run llama3.2 "Why is the sky blue?"
greenlens measure --pid 4242 --duration 5m
greenlens measure --unit ollama.service --duration 10m
```

## greenlens report

Report the energy measured by the agent in a period, by domain and in total, with its emissions and, when a tariff is configured, its cost. Periods can be dates, RFC 3339 times or amounts of time ago such as 24h or 7d.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens report [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--by` | Group by none, hour or day | `none` |
| `--from` | Start of the period | `24h` |
| `--to` | End of the period | `now` |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens report
greenlens report --from 7d --by day
greenlens report --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-11-01 --output csv
```

## greenlens setup-permissions

Show the changes that give the greenlens-power group read access to the RAPL energy counters, and optionally the IPMI device and the CAP_PERFMON capability for perf_event. Nothing changes until the command runs as root with --apply.

**Usage**

```text
greenlens setup-permissions [flags]
```

**Options**

| Option | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` | Apply the plan; needs root |  |
| `--ipmi` | Also give the group access to the IPMI device |  |
| `--perfmon` | Also grant CAP_PERFMON to this binary, for perf_event |  |
| `--user` | Add this user to the group |  |
| `--yes` | Do not ask for confirmation |  |

**Examples**

```bash
greenlens setup-permissions
sudo greenlens setup-permissions --apply --user $USER
sudo greenlens setup-permissions --apply --perfmon --ipmi
```

|---|---|---|
